FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 1 November 1988, after the draft finalized by the Silk, Man-made Fibre and Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This Indian Standard was first published in 1977 and has been revised on the basis of experience gained during its use. In the revised standard additional requirements for type of weave, length, dimensional change, colour fastness to washing, pH value of aqueous extract and sampling have been included. This standard prescribes tolerance in respect of linear density of warp and weft yarn, ends/dm, picks/dm, mass/m2, length and width of fabric keeping in view its end use and optimum quality. However, the Textile ( Consumer Protection ) Regulation, 1988 issued under clause 17 of the Textiles ( Control ) order 1986 specifies that the limits of variation on these requirements as laid down in Notifications issued under Section 95 of the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958, shall be applicable. In cases of dispute, the limits of variation as specified under the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958, shall prevail. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified i. value in this standard.

RAYONSATINLININGCLOTHFOR BERETS- SPECIFICATION (First Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of rayon satin lining cloth used in the manufacture of berets. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The India Standards listed in Annex A are necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 MANUFACTURE 3.1 Yarn Continuous filament viscose rayon yarn as per Grade I or Grade II of IS : 2427-1968 shall be used in the manufacture of lining cloth. The grade of the yarn used shall be as per agreement between the buyer and the seller. The yarn used may be dull, semi-dull or bright. 3.2 Cloth The cloth shall be well made and evenly woven in 5-end satin weave free from imperfections affecting its serviceability. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Constructional Particulars
The cloth shall

4.2 Dyeing If required, either the cloth or the yarns from which it is to be manufactured shall be dyed with suitable dyes to shades as agreed to between the buyer and the seller. Sulphur dyes shall not be used. The colour shall be as stated in the contract or the order.
4.2-l If dyed, the fabric shall conform to the colour fastness requirements as specified in Table 2.

4.3 pH Value of Aqueous Extract 4.3.1 The pH value of the aqueous extract of the cloth when tested by the hot method specified in IS 1390 : 1983 shall be 6'0 to 8'5. 4.4 Dimensional Change 4.4.1 The dimensional change of the fabric when tested according to the method specified in IS 1299 : 1984, shall not be more than 3 percent in each warp and weft direction. 5 MARKING 5.1 Each roll or piece of fabric shall be legibly marked with the following: 4 Name of material; b) Manufacturer's name, initial or trademark, if any; Length and width of roll or piece; 4 Date of manufacture; and d)

6 PACKlNG 6.1 The cloth shall be packed in accordance with the provisions of IS 2195 : 1964 or IS 2194 : 1963, as the case may be. 7 SAMPLING CONFORMITY 7.1 Lot The quantity of rayon satin lining cloth of the same quality and width delivered to a buyer agains one despatch note shall constitute a lot. 7.2 The conformity of the lot to the requirements of this standard shall be determined on the basis of tests carried out on the samples selected from the lot. 7.3 Unless otherwise agreed upon between the buyer and the seller, the number of pieces of cloth to be selected at random from a lot shall be in accordance with co1 2 of Table 3. 7.4 For of yarn, selected the test evaluating ( a ) mass ( b) linear density ( c ) width, and ( d ) length, the sample as in co1 2 of Table 3 shall constitute sample. In the case of length, the length of each piece is not less than the specified, declared or marked length, and if not the mean percentage of deficiency in length is determined and made applicable to the lot. From the observed values of the breaking load tests in respect of each piece in the test sample, the average breaking load value is calculated. From $1 such average values, the grand average X and the range R, is calcula_ted and the value of the expression X - 0'6 RI is found to be greater than or equal to the specified value.

The grand average 8. IS the value obtained by dividing the sum of the average breaking load value in respect of all the pieces in the test sample, by the number of pieces tested.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the proto ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standard3 Act, 1986 to promote harmonius development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Revision of Indian Standards Indian Standards are reviewed periodically and revised, when necessary and amendments, if any, are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition.
